questions.question: What is HyperLogLog?

options.text: A distributed logging framework for microservices
A probabilistic algorithm for estimating the cardinality (count of distinct elements) of large datasets
A sorting algorithm for streaming data
A data compression method for log files

questions.explanation: HyperLogLog: estimates count of unique elements using minimal memory. 12KB can estimate billions of unique items with ~2% error. Used for: unique visitors, distinct queries, cardinality estimation at scale.

questions.question: What problem does HyperLogLog solve?

options.text: Counting unique elements when storing all elements would require too much memory

questions.explanation: Problem: count unique visitors from 1 billion events. Exact: store all IDs (gigabytes). HyperLogLog: ~12KB, ~2% error. Tradeoff: small memory for approximate count. Acceptable for analytics.

questions.question: How does HyperLogLog work conceptually?

options.text: Hashes elements and uses the position of the leftmost 1-bit to estimate cardinality

questions.explanation: HyperLogLog intuition: hash each element, count leading zeros. Rare to see many leading zeros. If you see 10 leading zeros, probably saw ~2^10 unique elements. Uses multiple 'registers' and harmonic mean for accuracy.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of HyperLogLog?

options.text: O(n) where n is number of elements

questions.explanation: HyperLogLog: constant space. Standard implementation: 2^14 = 16384 registers, 6 bits each = 12KB. Can estimate cardinalities up to billions. Space doesn't grow with data size. Remarkable efficiency.

questions.question: What is the typical error rate of HyperLogLog?

options.text: About 0.81% to 2% standard error depending on configuration

questions.explanation: HyperLogLog error: ~1.04/√m where m is number of registers. With 16384 registers: ~0.81% standard error. Configurable: more registers = more accuracy = more memory. 2% error often acceptable for analytics.

questions.question: Can HyperLogLog structures be merged?

options.text: Yes—take maximum of each register, enabling distributed counting
Only if they're the same size

questions.explanation: HyperLogLog merge: take max of corresponding registers. Result estimates union cardinality. Enables: distributed counting (merge from multiple servers), time-window aggregation. Key feature for scalability.

questions.question: Which systems use HyperLogLog?
questions.explanation: HyperLogLog widely used: Redis (PFADD/PFCOUNT commands), PostgreSQL (cardinality estimation), Elasticsearch (cardinality aggregation), Presto, Spark, BigQuery. Standard tool for approximate distinct counts.

questions.question: What is the difference between HyperLogLog and exact counting?

options.text: HyperLogLog: O(1) space, approximate; Exact: O(n) space, precise

questions.explanation: Exact counting: store all unique elements (HashSet), O(n) space. HyperLogLog: O(1) space (~12KB), ~2% error. For 1 billion unique 8-byte IDs: exact = 8GB, HLL = 12KB. Massive difference.

questions.question: What are Redis PFADD and PFCOUNT commands?

options.text: HyperLogLog commands—PFADD adds elements, PFCOUNT returns estimated cardinality

questions.explanation: Redis HyperLogLog: PFADD key element (add to HLL), PFCOUNT key (get estimate), PFMERGE dest key1 key2 (merge HLLs). 'PF' honors Philippe Flajolet, HLL inventor. Simple API for powerful functionality.

questions.question: When should you NOT use HyperLogLog?

options.text: When you need exact counts or the cardinality is small enough to count exactly
When merging counts from multiple sources

questions.explanation: Don't use HyperLogLog when: exact count required (financial, compliance), cardinality is small (just use HashSet), need to enumerate elements (HLL only counts). Use when: large scale, approximate OK.

questions.question: What is the relationship between HyperLogLog registers and accuracy?

options.text: More registers = higher accuracy but more memory

questions.explanation: Accuracy tradeoff: error ≈ 1.04/√m. 1024 registers: ~3.25% error, 1.5KB. 16384 registers: ~0.81% error, 12KB. Choose based on accuracy needs and memory budget. Configurable.

questions.question: A website needs to count unique visitors per day. They get 100 million visits daily. Best approach?

options.text: Store all visitor IDs in a database
Use HyperLogLog—12KB per day gives ~2% accurate unique count

questions.explanation: 100M visits/day: storing IDs = gigabytes. HyperLogLog: 12KB/day, ~2% error. For 'how many unique visitors?' that's perfect. PFADD on each visit, PFCOUNT for result. Redis makes this trivial.
